extracts.lead_summary: The dollar won the argument I said copper was having with it. DXY closed 101.93 — a second weekly close above 101, 0.17 from the year's high — and copper lost my $6.60 rail, finishing near $6.49 (-3.0%). Gold fell 3.7%, silver 6.6%. The restriction on commodity longs stays ON. XLB did what the map said a failed reclaim would do: it closed under $49.57 on Monday, traded to $47.81 on Thursday on 25.6M shares, and finished at $48.86 (-1.9%), with Thursday's $48.54 the lowest close since late March. And the demand verdict I was waiting for came in on the bulls' side — ISM 54.5 — and did not matter. One housekeeping fact outranks all of that for anyone reading the tables: Corteva split in two on October 1, and its '-85%' is a spin-off, not a crash.
